rows.description: A preschooler chants rhymes, imitates animals and copies sound effects to play, practise language and share joy. Imitation is play, not mockery, unless it is aimed at hurting someone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child may sing softly to a toy or self when frightened, lonely or bored. Adults can honour it as a healthy coping tool and join in when the child invites.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, boredom, loneliness

rows.description: A preschooler learns to say hello, give a name and say thank you, often by adult prompting. Some children go quiet or hide behind a parent, which is shyness and can be respected.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: gratitude, admiration, shyness

rows.description: A child in many Indian families greets with namaste or touches elders' feet to show respect. Customs vary by region, family and faith, and a child who is unsure should be taught kindly, not shamed.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler describes a drawing or reports what happened at play, often with gaps and mixed-up order. Patient prompts like and then what help without making the child feel wrong.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young child narrates events with imagination and exaggeration, blending fantasy with fact. It is developmentally normal, so adults gently separate pretend from real when facts matter, without harsh labels.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young child learns to say I do not understand or say it again instead of guessing. Adults praise asking so a child does not feel shame about not knowing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler's repeated why questions signal curiosity, wanting attention or testing limits. Short honest answers or asking what the child thinks keep the dialogue alive without exhaustion.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Certainty and I do not know [Expressing]
rows.description: A preschooler often states things with total certainty and may not yet see the limits of own knowledge. Adults model saying I do not know, let us find out to show uncertainty is fine.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young child says really? or no way with wide eyes to show disbelief, and says it will be big to state expectation. Wishes and beliefs can blur, so adults gently separate what is hoped from what is known.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
